blocks.text: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, composed of several fused aromatic rings, are common environmental pollutants; naphthalene, anthracene and phenanthrene are examples. They are generated primarily during the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels (coal, oil, petrol and wood), in vehicle emissions and industrial processes, and even in grilled food; some come from natural sources such as open burning and the natural seepage of petroleum and coal deposits. They are potentially toxic and carcinogenic.
How do PAHs enter the atmosphere, and how do they affect human health?
